utterances.text: Depending on his answer, it may be very relevant, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What do you say, Mr. Domazet? Certainly he did not mention the place where he broke his leg or the particular time in cross-examination. Do you object to counsel for the Prosecution asking any questions about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if Mr. Groome considers that the question is important for him, then I have nothing against it; of course, if you allow this yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that's an answer or not. If you say you do not object to him doing it because Mr. Groome thinks it's important, then we, of course, will allow him to do it. If we have to rule upon it, it may be a different question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome. Further cross-examination by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lindo, can you tell us where you were treated for your broken leg?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: Me? You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember, were you treated in the hospital, and if so, which hospital?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: I just said a moment ago that I had broken my leg too. I broke it in the company I worked for, in 1989, and I was treated in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you break your leg in Blace?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: No. No. When you asked me about Mitar, when he broke his leg, I said I don't know, but I know what it's like when you break a leg, because I've broken a leg too. That's what I said. I have nothing further to add. I just said that I knew what it was like to break a leg because I had broken a leg too. Do you understand me? I'm not an eyewitness or anything. I just said, when you asked me whether I went up to ask him how he was, where he had broken a leg, I just said that I know what it's like to break a leg, and that's why I didn't ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is what appears at page 85, Mr. Groome, if you're looking for it. He --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1989. 1989.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please. Just one moment. He said, at line 12:

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: But actually, I had broken a leg too when I was doing guard duty in Prelovo. Those were different conditions. I was transferred there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were transferred later from Blace; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: Yes. Is that what you're thinking of?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lindo, you've just heard the Court read your testimony from just a few minutes ago. Did you or did you not break your leg while you were on guard duty in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: No. No. What I said was, when the Judge asked me whether I knew him when he broke his leg, and I said that I don't know when he broke his leg but that I broke a leg in 1989 and I know what it feels like when you break a leg. That's what I said. I don't know what else. I didn't say that I was on guard duty here or there. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one final question. If you had -- if somebody had broken their leg in Prelovo, would I be correct in saying that the nearest hospital, or the hospital they would have been brought to, would have been Uzice hospital? Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA LINDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any re-examination on that, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir, for coming along to give evidence here. We're very grateful to you for coming and for the evidence you've given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you please make the solemn declaration which is in the document that the Court usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Take his headset off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to take this off. Shall I read it aloud? I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Please sit down, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Tanaskovic. Examined by Mr. Tanaskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vojinovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your name, first and last.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I am Vasilije Vojinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us when and where you were born.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Vlasina, near Visegrad, in 1935, on the 24th of April - that's what my parents told me - on Easter day, and that's why they gave me the name Vasilije.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to caution you to pause between my question and your answer, because the interpreters can't keep up with us. So I'm saying this so that the President of the Chamber need not interrupt the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you didn't, since you didn't make a pause in answer to my first question. Tell me, please, where you are living now and what you do for a living. What is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a cook by occupation, and I am now in the village of Blace, near Visegrad. I am retired and I'm working the land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you used to work as a cook and retired as such?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which company?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in Belgrade, in Zegrep, in the Sarajevo Zegrep, but the branch office in Belgrade; headquartered in Sarajevo but with a branch office in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you work in that company?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I worked there for 24 years, in the same company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you lived in Belgrade during those 24 years?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you come to visit your native region?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did visit, as my family were in the villages, the children were at school, my wife and mother were in the village. Sometimes it would be after a month, sometimes a month and a half, I would go back home to visit them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would go home after a month or after a month and a half; it depended?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you are now living in the village of Blace.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know Mr. Vasiljevic, Mitar?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: He went to school when he was younger, and he would pass by my house as he travelled from his village to the bus stop, until he completed -- I assume it was his eight-year elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: What is the name of his village?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: His village is called Djurevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is that village of Djurevici from your village?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe three or three and a half kilometres. You go over a hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you knew that family, the whole Vasiljevic family?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I do know them, because we are not far from one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, or rather, tell us: Have you done your military service?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was in the former Yugoslav People's Army, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: In Pozarevac for six months, and then I was transferred to Pirot on the -- to the Bulgarian border, the village of Toplje Do [phoen]. I was at the guardhouse there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your speciality or what branch of the army were you? Please, Mr. Vojinovic. Wait a moment and then give us your answer. Go on.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I was a border guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a cook in the army?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I was a border guard in the army, and then I went to Dimitrovgrad to attend a cooking and baking course, because there was a bakery at the border which was far removed from the town. So I had to complete this course for a cook and baker at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us a moment ago that you were a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you retire?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid I can't remember what year it was. I've forgot. I am a bit nervous, so I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a different question. Since when have you been permanently residing in Blace, in your village? When did you stop working in Belgrade? Wait a moment, please. Please, Vojinovic. Go on.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I have been in Blace since 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the Uzice Corps left, there was a mobilisation. Were you mobilised and by whom?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I was, by the Territorial Defence, whatever it's called. I was mobilised as a cook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you assigned to?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I was assigned to Prelovo, to the school building there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain what the school building contained?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: It used to be the elementary school, eight-year elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not what I meant. I was asking you what was organised in that building to which you were assigned. Please wait, Mr. Vojinovic. Look at the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is not switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Switch it on to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: What had been organised in that school building to which you had been assigned? You can go on.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: In that school building a kitchen was set up, and there were refugees. This was a large hall, and there were a lot of refugees. And we were given two rooms for the storage and for the kitchen, a storeroom and a kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this kitchen, who was it meant for, or rather, who did you prepare food for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you some trouble in answering the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid of making a mistake. We prepared food there for the army, for the Territorial Defence. I can't even speak it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, who was working in that kitchen, all the people who were working there?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence asked me to go there to be the cook, as I had been a cook in the army too. And there was a Mitrasin there, Mitrasin Glisic, who was cleaning. Dragisa Lindo, he helped us. He cleaned the compound and brought firewood for the stoves which we cooked on. We had very limited resources. And they cleaned around. And I prepared the meals for the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the Chamber to clearly understand what you mean, what do you mean when you say "lines"?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: It's for the troops. The army of the Territorial Defence that was on the war front, that was deployed on the front lines. And then cauldrons of food were being prepared, breakfast and lunch. The dinner was sometimes dry-packed rations because it was a long distance across mountains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned Dragisa Lindo, Mitrasin, yourself. Was anyone else there with you?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: If we needed to peel potatoes, to clean the beans, they would give us some other people who were unfit for going to the front line. Then they would be assigned to us as necessary, when that was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, who was the chief of the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, Mitar Vasiljevic told us what each one of us was to do and how many cauldrons should be sent where and the numerical composition of the troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the duties of each of these persons that you mentioned. What did Mr. Vasiljevic do? What was his duty?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: He provided foodstuffs, and as the kitchen was not in order, he supplied us with the pots and food because this wasn't something that was clean and regulated and in order. So he was with us. Sometimes he would go into the field with the troops to assist them for the time that he was with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he brought in supplies. Tell us, how did he do that?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: He would go into town. The Territorial Defence, whatever they had, they sent us. Sometimes it was cabbages, sometimes beans, sometimes macaroni. The situation was bad. And what they had, what was available, he brought it and we prepared it. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were those provisions brought from Visegrad or from wherever? What was used? Wait a moment, Vojinovic, please. Look at the screen in front of you. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Sumarstvo gave us a van, and they drove the food in that van. And when we prepared the meals, again the same van would deliver them, deliver the food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The van you mentioned, was it requisitioned too or mobilised?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Well, surely it must have been requisitioned when it was used to transport the food. Sometimes it had a red marking, sometimes a green one. When it went into the field, they changed these colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain what markings you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to put it. I suppose on the basis of some kind of military secret, so that somebody would not intercept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vojinovic, do you know the driver of the van?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Obren Vojinovic. He used to work in the Sumarstvo company, and the van belonged to that company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you explained what the duties were of Mr. Vasiljevic and what he was doing in that kitchen. Among other things, you mentioned that he procured the food. Did he do so using this van you mentioned and the driver that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: There was another van, and one would go in one direction and the other in the other direction, because they couldn't make it with one van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, we are talking about the van with which foodstuffs were transported from the Territorial Defence, as you told us. Now, which van are you talking about? The one that was driven by Vojinovic or some other van?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes [redacted] would drive it. That was his surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did [redacted] drive?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: He drove foodstuffs like this other one. My duties were in the kitchen. I didn't go out much. I don't know what people were doing outside the kitchen, because I couldn't move away from the pots. The firewood wasn't dry. It was difficult to cook the food, and it was my duty to cook it properly for the people who spent days and nights in the mountains. So I couldn't see or hear anyone or talk to anyone. I was busy all the time around the stoves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vojinovic, who drove the food when the kitchen was in Blace?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: When the kitchen was in Blace, the driver was [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that Mr. Vasiljevic was the one who appointed you specifically as the cook. Tell us: Were you issued any kind of weapon, and if so, which?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I asked from the Territorial Defence that I be given a weapon because I had to travel home seven kilometres during the night. My wife was alone. There was a war on, and it wasn't safe, so I had to go to check on her to make sure she was all right. So I carried this weapon. Fortunately, I never had any problems, because it's seven kilometres, the distance through the woods to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vojinovic, would you please answer my questions, the specific questions I'm asking you. My next question is: What weapon were you issued, and who issued it to you?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I was given an automatic rifle from the Territorial Defence. A soldier brought it to me in the kitchen. I asked him to bring it to me because I was travelling at night. I was afraid. I didn't dare cross the mountains on my way home unarmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: How frequently would you go home from the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: VASILIJE VOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Every other evening, as my wife was alone at home. She was afraid. And I would come back at 3.00 or half past 3.00 a.m. so as to have enough time to prepare the food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's 4.00, Mr. Tanaskovic. We'll adjourn now until 9.30 in the morning. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.
